title: Hull insurance: vessel structure and equipment
excerpt: Hull, machinery, values and lay-up stages are distinct from CARGO and P&I. Prepare vessel interests and records for assessment.

seo.title: Hull insurance: vessel and equipment assessment | ING Broker
seo.description: Prepare vessel identity, ownership, equipment, values, use, navigation areas and workshop periods separately from cargo and liability.
seo.keywords: Hull insurance Moldova, vessel hull, marine insurance, vessel equipment inventory, Hull CARGO P&I

content:
Hull is the name used when assessing insurance for a vessel's hull and components identified in the contract. It differs from insurance for transported goods and the operator's liability to other people. For a company with maritime interests in the Republic of Moldova, start with the vessel, owner, actual use and documented values. The English product name alone does not establish protection.

This informational article confirms no Hull solution through ING Broker for every vessel, flag or area. The Naval Agency of the Republic of Moldova publishes distinct services for maritime and inland vessels and relevant documents. Registration, certification and operating requirements need separate verification. This text interprets no conventions, establishes no legal obligations and provides no navigation or repair instructions.

Which vessel and interest are being assessed?

Prepare the exact identity from vessel records and the relationships between owner, operator and any financier. The applicant does not necessarily have the same interest as every other party. Examine any lease or use agreement separately. The capacity in which each entity appears in a proposal needs an explanation, rather than an assumption that all parties share one interest or one potential payment.

Describe vessel type and actual activity, not an internet example in place of your own information. Two vessels of equal value may perform different services and need different questions. Identify the competent person or organization able to confirm technical records. The broker does not certify technical condition, seaworthiness or operating rights. An insurance discussion therefore cannot replace those separate professional checks.

Hull, machinery and components need an inventory

Resolve what the vessel includes through the proposed contract's definition and inventory. Separate hull, installations, machinery and other relevant components. Spares aboard or elsewhere may need distinct enquiries. Not every item bought for the vessel is automatically part of the same value or protection. Ask about its actual identity, location and treatment instead of assuming a general vessel description settles the question.

Document important components through identifiers and value evidence. Link changes or replacements to technical records. An administrative inventory does not replace expert assessment, but prevents confusion between items. If a proposal uses a general definition, ask how it applies to the specific property being considered. Keep the response connected to the version reviewed so a later replacement is not silently treated as already accepted.

Transported cargo requires separate assessment

Vessel and cargo represent different interests, even when one company has a commercial connection with both. A Hull assessment does not establish cargo insurance. CARGO should not be considered vessel-hull protection either. Identify who owns the goods and who is responsible for transport under actual documents. A product name alone supplies no legal conclusion about that relationship.

Where a transport agreement sets special requirements, retain its exact wording for review. Do not assume an obligation transfers completely to an insurer. Property protection, cargo liability and particular incident expenses require distinct checking. This remains useful even if components are later discussed within a combined programme. A shared commercial discussion does not make every proposed component accepted or interchangeable.

Describe the navigation area precisely

Prepare proposed areas and activity without publishing sensitive routes. Neither the vessel's flag nor the insurer's country establishes acceptance of an area. A route change may require another documentary check. Requirements of ports, authorities and jurisdictions need competent specialists. Do not generalize an article about Moldova into confirmation of every external requirement affecting a journey or operation.

Do not publish a presumed list of accepted countries instead of actual terms. Identify restrictions and unclear points before a commercial decision. Insurance authorizes no operation and replaces no vessel documents. A reply about contractual territory does not automatically confirm every external requirement. Keep the insurance answer distinct from permission, technical certification and any other competent checks required for the activity.

Vessel value and financing

Separate property value, loan balance and planned investment costs. Prepare dated evidence for the value being discussed. The purchase price should not be assumed appropriate regardless of modifications, age or configuration. Ask about the proposal's valuation basis and any financier's interest. Different financial figures must remain identifiable rather than being added into one unexplained amount merely because they relate to the same vessel.

For later components, update the inventory and ask whether insurance documents need amendment. A new invoice alone does not confirm inclusion. Possible compensation cannot be inferred from total company expenditure. It depends on the contract, event and supporting file, examined by the insurer under applicable conditions. Keep confirmed values separate from amounts only requested or still awaiting assessment.

Lay-up, yards and service providers

A vessel can pass through operating, lay-up and work periods. Describe dates and provider relationships without technical instructions. A yard handover or repair should not automatically be treated like normal use. Ask which stages are relevant and document changes before assuming protection is unchanged. A planned period and a confirmed current arrangement should remain distinguishable in the file.

A provider's policy does not automatically establish protection for the vessel or owner. Contracts can allocate responsibilities requiring specialist review. Retain handover records, work descriptions and communication roles. Do not convert those records into a conclusion about fault or an unexamined claim payment. The fact that a provider participated does not decide who bears every consequence of an incident.

Liability and P&I are not synonyms for Hull

Other people's demands, certain operating obligations and further exposures may need assessment separate from vessel property. P&I refers to protection and indemnity, but actual content depends on the documents considered. It is not a universal supplement for everything omitted by Hull. Product terminology cannot fill an unanswered question about a particular person, expense or contractual obligation.

Maintain separate categories for own property, third-party property, people and contractual duties. For each, identify the document reviewed and what remains unconfirmed. Keep unavailable or unaccepted components visible. Do not describe a programme internally as everything included without actual confirmations. A short summary must preserve the limits, not remove them to make the proposal sound simpler or more complete.

Separate incident expenses by their nature

Property repair, auxiliary expenses and lost income can have different treatment. Do not automatically add delay or non-performance of a commercial agreement to vessel value. Explain each need and ask about availability and conditions. This article confirms no salvage, removal, interruption or other special expense protection. A preparation list should identify questions rather than present every possible expense as a benefit.

Economic dependencies are still useful for planning. Identify external services and relevant continuity periods while keeping operations separate from insurance. An alternative plan does not establish risk acceptance, and a policy does not replace planning. Financial information and commercial contracts should use the secure assessment channel agreed with appropriate recipients. General discussion need not expose an entire confidential commercial archive.

How to compare the proposed documents

Read the identified vessel, interests, use, area and period first. Then examine events, exclusions and limits. Exclusions describe situations outside the contract's protection. The excess is the insured's share of a loss under the terms. Similar expressions in two proposals do not establish identical conditions. Ask about differences relevant to the real vessel and activity rather than interpreting one document through another.

The insurance premium is the amount paid for the policy. Compare prices using the same value, activity and period. Check notification and incident documents from the applicable wording without importing another product's deadlines. The broker can help structure comparison within its mandate. It does not take over the insurer's decision to accept risk or obligation to examine and pay a claim under the contract.

Example: updating a vessel inventory

Imagine an owner replacing an important component and changing a planned lay-up period. Prepare separate records for the asset change and use. The invoice and unchanged vessel identifier do not confirm that insurance documents remain suitable. This is a hypothetical illustration, not an ING Broker customer or a real vessel. It supplies no repair instruction or assessment of the component's technical fitness.

The company retains communication chronology and the reply concerning each change. If no clear reply exists, the point stays open. This prevents the mistaken conclusion that any vessel-related expenditure belongs to Hull. Administrative discipline does not replace technical, legal or contractual review. Its purpose is traceability, not automatic acceptance or a promise of a particular financial outcome.

A preparation file for Hull assessment

  • Vessel identification and entities with an interest.
  • Relevant records checked with competent specialists.
  • Inventory of hull, installations and components discussed.
  • Values and their supporting evidence.
  • Activity, areas and lay-up or work stages.
  • Provider relationships and contractual requirements.
  • Changes, known incidents and unconfirmed points.

Follow components moving between vessel and workshop

A component may be removed for checking and remain temporarily in a workshop while another takes its place. Record item, serial reference, owner, destination and handover evidence. Do not assume identical treatment everywhere. Ask about relevant stages without claiming transport or works are included. Keep the original property record linked to its current location and status rather than treating removal as an unexplained disappearance.

Separate component value from the bill for services performed on it. Maintenance expenditure and loss of the item are different questions. If several vessels share a spare, avoid counting its full value as installed on each vessel simultaneously. Records should identify the actual place and interest through responsible people's verified documents. A supplier's service fee should not silently become the component's accepted property value.

When the inventory is restored, retain the change sheet and insurance reply. Do not remove the original record: it explains the earlier declaration. This also helps renewal by showing current configuration instead of a list copied year after year. Historical records remain history, while the current version identifies what is now present and which insurance questions still await an answer.

Frequently asked questions about Hull

Does Hull automatically cover cargo?

No. Vessel property and cargo are different interests. Check each contract's subject rather than inferring cargo protection from the existence of a vessel policy.

Are all components bought later included?

Do not assume so. Update the inventory and request documentary checking. A new purchase does not automatically establish inclusion or acceptance of its value.

Does Hull replace P&I?

Do not treat them as synonyms. Vessel property and particular liability demands need separate assessment. Availability and conditions of each component require individual confirmation.

Does a policy establish a right to operate?

No. Competent authorities and specialists check vessel documents and operating requirements separately. Insurance assessment does not replace applicable authorization or certification.

Next step

Request a discussion with ING Broker about assessment and intermediation possibilities. The broker explains options and arranges insurance where possible; the insurer decides acceptance and claims under the contract. This guide confirms neither product availability nor coverage of an individual case.
